iteration_summaries.hypothesis: The system has 6 active inputs (X1-X6) and 6 inert inputs (X7-X12). The system is fundamentally MULTIPLICATIVE with regime-switching effects. Y1 is driven by X2×X4 synergy (28x amplification) with X5 as binary threshold gate (~0.4), X1/X3 as saturating multipliers, and X6 as positive accelerating contributor modulated by X2 and X4. Y2 has a REGIME SWITCH at X2≈0.74 for X6's effect: below crossover X6 worsens Y2, above it X6 helps Y2. Y2 is also increased by X2, decreased by X1/X3, with X4 context-dependent. Y3 = f(X1)·g(X3) depends only on X1 and X3 (both positive, saturating). Y4 = synergistic function of X2×X4 minus X6 penalty, with weak X1 positive contribution. The Pareto front is a 2D surface parameterized by (X2, X6) with X1=X3=X4=1 and X5≥0.5 universally optimal. At X2≈0.74, X6 is a free Y1 booster (zero Y2 cost), creating a sweet spot. X4=1 is always optimal because X4→Y2 gradient is convex (diminishing Y2 benefit from reduction) while X4→Y4 is concave (increasing Y4 cost from reduction). Model predictions consistently within 0.5-1% error across 10+ validation points in final optimization phase.
new_findings: All 5 final optimization points joined the Pareto front, expanding it from 32 to 37 non-dominated solutions
Hypervolume improved from 0.2671 to 0.2678 by filling mid-range Y2 gaps at X2=0.36 and X2=0.49 with X6 boost
Model predictions achieved <0.7% error on all 5 final points: max Y1 error 0.005, max Y2 error 0.007, max Y4 error 0.002
At X2=0.36, X6 boost from 0.1→1.0 increases Y1 from 0.238 to 0.608 (+156%) while Y2 only increases from 0.132 to 0.210 (+59%), confirming favorable Y1/Y2 trade-off ratio even below the regime switch
At X2=0.49, X6 boost from 0.1→1.0 increases Y1 from 0.358 to 0.698 (+95%) while Y2 increases from 0.171 to 0.226 (+32%), even more favorable ratio
Y4 penalty from X6 is roughly constant: ~0.07 reduction per 0.9 units of X6 across all X2 levels tested
The Pareto front now spans Y1=[0.049, 1.132], Y2=[0.071, 0.362], Y4=[0.036, 0.322] with 37 well-distributed non-dominated points
surprises: Y2 systematic slight underestimation by 0.005-0.007 in all 5 final points suggests a small nonlinear correction term in the X6→Y2 relationship that my linear gradient model doesn't capture

Despite X6→Y2 being positive at X2=0.36 (gradient +0.067), the Y1/Y2 ratio of 6.4:1 still makes X6 boost worthwhile for Pareto expansion, which I initially didn't expect to be effective below the X2=0.74 crossover

The hypervolume gain of 0.0007 from 5 carefully placed points is modest, suggesting the front was already quite well-populated and further gains require either novel input combinations or discovering missed nonlinearities
